summary: Updates some entries in the IANA registry of cryptographic algorithms used by DNSSEC, which signs DNS data. It adjusts how particular algorithm entries are described. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: DNSSEC uses numbered algorithms to sign DNS data. RFC 6725 changes three unused placeholder numbers to Reserved to avoid conflicts with older implementations.

questions: which dnssec algorithm numbers are reserved
why were dnssec algorithm 4 9 and 11 reserved
subtitle: Reserves three DNSSEC algorithm numbers and updates registry references.

tldr.problem: Three DNSSEC algorithm numbers had been set aside for algorithms that were not fully specified, which could conflict with older implementations.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC changes the descriptions for assignments 4, 9, and 11 to Reserved and updates references in the registry.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6725 is a Proposed Standard and updates the DNSSEC algorithm registry entries.

facts.label: Other entries
facts.value: Unchanged except for listed reference updates

today: RFC 6725 is a Proposed Standard from August 2012. The unit metadata records no later RFC as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: DNSSEC Algorithm Numbers
sections.content:
DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC) use digital signatures over DNS data to provide source authentication and integrity protection. An IANA registry lists codes for signature algorithms, each combining an asymmetric cryptographic algorithm with a one-way hash function.

This memo updates selected entries in the DNSSEC Algorithm Numbers registry and refreshes references. The auxiliary sub-registries for Diffie-Hellman parameters are unchanged.
sections.plainLanguage: DNSSEC signs DNS data, and a registry assigns numbers to the signing algorithms. This RFC changes a few entries in that list.

sections.title: Numbers Changed to Reserved
sections.content:
The descriptions for algorithm numbers 4, 9, and 11 are changed to Reserved. They had been placeholders for algorithms that were not fully specified for DNSSEC use.

The RFC gives the reason: older implementations may still have these codes assigned. Reserving the numbers is intended to prevent potential incompatibilities. Other existing entries are unchanged, except for the listed reference updates.
sections.plainLanguage: Numbers 4, 9, and 11 are marked Reserved because older software may treat them as assigned. The rest of the entries remain unchanged by this document.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo updates a registry and does not discuss which cryptographic algorithms are superior. It states that the document raises no new security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: This registry update does not assess algorithm strength. The RFC says it raises no new security considerations.
